summary: Build-config change to the published @cipherstash/stack package: the type declarations for the ESM-only `./wasm-inline` entry are now emitted by the main dual-format tsup config, so they share the column-class declaration chunk with `./eql/v3`, `./v3` and `./adapter-kit`. The JS bundle for wasm-inline is unchanged. The result is that tables authored from either entry now typecheck against the other entry and against adapter `schemas` types. Shipped agent skills (copied into customer repos by `stash`) are rewritten to recommend sharing one schema module across entries, and a text guard that enforced the old rule is deleted and replaced by new dist-level type gates that run in CI. There is no runtime code change apart from an error-message string. I found no `instanceof` checks on stack classes in any package source, so the runtime cross-entry use the docs now encourage still goes through the existing structural checks. The main risk is the published `dist/wasm-inline.d.ts` shape, a type-level contract. The new gates cover it and CI runs them, but I did not see a result. Smaller risks are doc and version skew in shipped skills and a contradictory pending changeset. Impact is medium and verification is medium. A focused review of the emitted declarations is recommended.

behaviour_changes.description: `dist/wasm-inline.d.ts` is now produced by the main config's DTS pass (`dts.entry` = main entries + `src/wasm-inline.ts`), and the wasm-inline config sets `dts: false`. The declarations now reference the shared `types-public-*.d.ts` chunk instead of inlining a private copy of every column class. A new unreferenced `dist/wasm-inline.d.cts` is also emitted.

Type-level contract: tables and columns authored with `encryptedTable`/`types` from `@cipherstash/stack/wasm-inline` become assignable to `AnyV3Table` from `./eql/v3` (and therefore to adapter `schemas`), and native-authored tables are accepted by the WASM `Encryption`. Before, both directions failed with a private-member nominal mismatch.

Shipped skills (stash-edge, stash-encryption, stash-managed-platforms, stash-supabase) reverse their guidance. They now say one schema module may be authored from either entry and passed to either client or to `encryptedSupabase`, with a note that older stack versions reject this.

The text guard `scripts/__tests__/skills-supabase-edge-schema-entry.test.mjs`, which failed if shipped docs paired wasm-inline tables with `encryptedSupabase`, is deleted. New compile-only gates over the emitted `dist/` (`dist-types/wasm-inline-type-identity.ts`, additions to `dist-types/node16/wasm-inline.mts`) assert identity in both directions. `logger-edge-safety.test.ts` now throws when `dist/` is missing under `CI`. Two error-matcher assertions are tightened.
The `[supabase v3]` EQL-v2-table construction error message now also names `@cipherstash/stack/wasm-inline` as a valid authoring entry. Message text only; the throw condition is unchanged.

failure_scenarios.title: Published dist/wasm-inline.d.ts is incomplete or wrong after moving DTS emission into the dual-format config
failure_scenarios.trigger: Release build of @cipherstash/stack with the new tsup config. The DTS rollup over 11 entries re-partitions shared chunks, and the wasm-inline entry's declarations (WasmEncryptionClient, Encryption overloads, Wasm* types, re-exports of `@/eql/v3`, external `@cipherstash/protect-ffi/wasm-inline` and `@cipherstash/auth/wasm-inline` types) are now emitted alongside the native entries.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: Before, `dist/wasm-inline.d.ts` came from a separate self-contained DTS pass (base tsup.config.ts). Now it is emitted by the main config (`dts: { entry: [...mainEntry, 'src/wasm-inline.ts'] }`, tsup.config.ts:52) and imports shared chunks. Any difference in how that pass resolves or names the wasm-inline exports, such as a declaration landing in a chunk the `.d.ts` does not re-export, or chunk-name changes, alters the type surface that edge consumers resolve through `exports['./wasm-inline'].import.types`. The JS stays on the old pass (`dts: false`, :78), so types and JS now come from two different builds.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Edge and Deno/Workers/Supabase consumers on TypeScript get compile errors or missing or `any`-widened types after upgrading. A widened schema type would weaken typed `encryptQuery`/domain checks without a runtime signal. Fixing it needs a new npm release.

failure_scenarios.title: Shipped skills recommend cross-entry schemas to customers whose installed @cipherstash/stack predates the fix
failure_scenarios.trigger: A customer upgrades `stash` (which carries skills/ and copies them into the repo) but keeps an older `@cipherstash/stack`, which the optional peer range `>=1.0.0-rc.0` allows. Their coding agent then follows the new example that authors `schemas` from `@cipherstash/stack/wasm-inline` for `encryptedSupabase`.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: skills/stash-edge/SKILL.md:384-450 and the other three skills now present wasm-inline authoring as correct. The fallback note refers only to 'older versions' and 'a version predating that fix' and names no version, so neither an agent nor a human can check applicability.
failure_scenarios.consequence: `tsc` fails with the private-member error on older stacks, and the agent may reach for `as any`, which the skills themselves warn against. The failure is loud and compile-time. Runtime behaviour is unaffected because adapters probe columns structurally.
missing_verification: No check ties the skill text to a minimum @cipherstash/stack version.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Name the first @cipherstash/stack version containing the fix in the 'older versions' notes once it is known, or raise the stash peer floor.

failure_scenarios.title: Pending changeset contradicts the new guidance in the same release's changelog
failure_scenarios.trigger: The next release consumes both `.changeset/supabase-docs-wasm-inline-entry.md` and `.changeset/wasm-inline-type-identity.md`.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: supabase-docs-wasm-inline-entry.md:49-58 states that wasm-inline-authored schemas do not compile with `encryptedSupabase`, that schemas must come from `eql/v3`, and that a guard (`skills-supabase-edge-schema-entry.test.mjs`) enforces this. This change deletes that guard and reverses the rule, but leaves that changeset unedited.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Published CHANGELOGs for stash and @cipherstash/stack-supabase carry two contradictory statements and reference a test that no longer exists, which confuses readers. This is documentation only.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Amend the earlier pending changeset, or note in the new one that it supersedes that guidance.

evidence.claim: The main dual-format config now emits declarations for `src/wasm-inline.ts` via `dts: { entry: [...mainEntry, 'src/wasm-inline.ts'] }`, and the comment notes an extra unreferenced `dist/wasm-inline.d.cts`.
The ESM-only wasm-inline config keeps JS emission with `noExternal` bundling but sets `dts: false` (it was a separate dts pass at base).
The `./wasm-inline` export has only an `import` branch, with types `./dist/wasm-inline.d.ts`.
The new compile-only gate asserts that wasm-inline tables and columns are assignable to `AnyV3Table`, and that both `Encryption` factories accept tables from either entry.
The node16 gate resolves both entries by package name and asserts cross-entry assignability in both directions.
`test:types:dist` depends on `build`, so the gate typechecks freshly emitted declarations.
`stash` declares `@cipherstash/stack` as a peer dependency `>=1.0.0-rc.0` (optional), so shipped skills can sit next to an older stack.
The skill now says schema modules cross entries and shows wasm-inline-authored tables passed to `encryptedSupabase`. The fallback refers to 'older versions' without naming one.
The pending changeset states that wasm-inline schemas do not compile with `encryptedSupabase` and cites the guard `skills-supabase-edge-schema-entry.test.mjs`.
The new changeset (patch for stack, stack-supabase, stash) describes the type-identity fix and says the runtime was unaffected.
The test now throws at module scope when `dist/adapter-kit.js` is missing and `CI` is set, instead of silently skipping.
`isV3ColumnLike` is a structural probe, not `instanceof`, so wasm-authored columns are recognised at runtime.
No `instanceof` checks against non-builtin classes exist in any package source at head, so the cross-entry runtime use the docs now encourage relies on structural checks.
The deleted guard enforced the old rule (wasm-inline schemas must not be paired with `encryptedSupabase` in shipped docs).
Only the error message text changed. It now also names `@cipherstash/stack/wasm-inline`.

`packages/stack/tsup.config.ts` usually changes with `packages/stack/package.json` (17 commits, conf 0.85) but package.json is unchanged here. I checked the exports map, and it needs no change for `./wasm-inline` types.
